summary: This paper develops and validates a frequency-shift measurement setup for superconducting radio-frequency cavities, enabling precision determination of resonance frequency and quality factor during warm-up from 5 K to 12 K across the superconducting-to-normal transition. The setup quantifies electron mean free paths in both regimes and characterizes an anomalous frequency dip near $T_c$ in mid-temperature heat-treated niobium cavities, with recent upgrades reducing measurement uncertainty to ~25% of empirical drifts and achieving spatial temperature gradients as low as ~2 K/m.
motivation: Understanding the superconducting properties of niobium cavities, particularly those intentionally modified by interstitial oxygen and nitrogen doping via mid-T heat treatments, requires study across the full temperature range rather than only at 2 K operation, especially given unexplained phenomena like the anti-Q-slope and anomalous frequency dips near $T_c$.
method: A dedicated cryostat apparatus measures transmitted $S_{21}$ spectra every minute during non-adiabatic warm-up with constant pressure regulation; resonance frequency and loaded quality factor $Q_L$ are extracted via Lorentzian fitting of power spectra; mechanical stress artifacts are mitigated by loosening cavity-mounting screws, and systematic empirical frequency-drift corrections are applied to account for transient thermal non-equilibrium; electron mean free paths are derived from surface resistance at 10 K and penetration-depth shifts via Eqs. 8–9.
result: Baseline niobium cavities yield $T_c \approx 9.29$ K from frequency shifts (agreeing with literature 9.27 K), while mid-T heat-treated cavities show suppressed $T_c$, larger total frequency shifts $\Delta f_{\max}$, and a reliable anomalous dip feature near $T_c$; mean free paths in the normal-conducting skin depth range from $\ell_\delta > 440$ nm (baseline) to $\ell_\delta < 75$ nm (mid-T treated), enabling oxygen-concentration estimates via $C_{O,\delta}$ and $C_{O,\lambda}$ using the resistivity-oxygen relationship of $4.5 \times 10^{-8}$ Ω·m·at.%$^{-1}$.
